findings.title: Cron deletes reminders whose scheduled date has passed before cancelling them
findings.body: The existing `deleteMany` for all EMAIL reminders with `scheduledDate <= now` runs before the new cancellation query. A cancelled reminder whose date falls within the last cron interval is already gone. The cancellation window is the next hour, but the cron runs every 15 minutes, so for emails scheduled between cron runs it is mostly fine. However, if a cron run is missed or delayed, SendGrid is never told to cancel and the email is sent. Cancellation should run before this delete, or the delete should exclude cancelled rows.

findings.title: One SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of all remaining reminders
findings.body: The loop awaits `client.request` inside a single try/catch. If one request fails (e.g. a bad batch_id or the 100-pending-cancellation limit), the loop exits and every later reminder is skipped until the next run. Nothing is deleted from the DB either, because `Promise.all` is never reached, even for reminders already cancelled at SendGrid. Handle errors per reminder. Also, `remindersToCancel` has no `method: EMAIL` filter and could include SMS reminders that have no valid batch id.

findings.title: SendGrid client API key is never set in the cron handler
findings.body: This file calls `client.request`, but only `sgMail.setApiKey` is called at the top. `client.setApiKey` is called in emailReminderManager, and the cron handler already relies on `client.request` for `/v3/mail/batch`. It works only if that module happens to be imported in the same process. Set the key explicitly here.

findings.title: Reminder with no referenceId is deleted even if scheduled and not yet sent, and unscheduled rows never get a cancel
findings.body: When `referenceId` is null the row is deleted, which is correct for unscheduled reminders. For scheduled reminders that are marked cancelled but later fall inside the 72h cron flow, cancellation relies on the cron only seeing `cancelled: true` rows. Unscheduled cancelled rows are removed immediately, so that case is fine. But `immediateDelete` cancels at SendGrid yet never deletes or marks the DB row. The stale reminder stays and is later removed only by the past-date cleanup.

findings.title: Reminder deletion promises are not awaited
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async but called without await or collection into the `Promise.all`. Previously the DB deletes were awaited. Now the handler can return, and a serverless runtime may freeze, before the DB update or delete or the Twilio cancel completes. Reminders may then stay uncancelled and still be sent. The same applies to bookings.tsx, handleNewBooking.ts and workflows.tsx.

findings.title: Workflow delete only handles scheduled reminders with immediateDelete, leaving cascade race
findings.body: On workflow delete, the immediate SendGrid cancel is fired un-awaited and then the workflow is deleted, which cascades to the reminders. The `immediateDelete` path never touches the DB row, which is fine, but errors are only logged and the request is not blocked. This is also what consumes the 100-cancellation limit the PR is trying to avoid.

findings.title: Unrelated reformatting inside commented-out block
findings.body: The diff strips indentation across a large commented-out testAction block. It is noise unrelated to the fix and makes review and blame harder. The `Prisma` and `PrismaPromise` imports were also changed from type imports to value imports without need.
